components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Secondary Button

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Standard text input. Stroke border, teal focus ring, error state.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; } .ds-label { font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #334155; } .ds-required { color: #dc2626; margin-left: 2px; } .ds-input { width: 100%; border: 1px solid #cbd5e1; border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; font-family: Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #1e293b; background: #ffffff; transition: border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #94a3b8; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #0f5c5c; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #1a9e9e33; } .ds-input:disabled { background: #f8fafc; color: #64748b; cursor: not-allowed; }

narrative.overview:
KaironTherapy is a clinical management tool built around the same values as the practitioners who use it: precision, care, and reliability. Every screen is a page in a well-kept patient record — organized, legible, nothing out of place. The design's job is to surface the right information at the right moment without demanding attention for itself.

The visual vocabulary is grounded rather than decorative. The Deep Forest Teal brand color anchors the system as trustworthy and calm. Neutral slate surfaces carry the data. Semantic colors communicate status clearly, without visual noise. Motion is restrained to functional feedback.

This system explicitly rejects the aesthetic of hospital EHR software — the gray overload, tiny inputs, and form-nightmare density. It equally rejects consumer wellness aesthetics and generic SaaS minimalism.
keyCharacteristics: Teal-anchored, slate-neutral palette — warm professional without being corporate blue
Information density calibrated to clinical workflows — structured but not overwhelming
Tactile and confident interactions — clear hover states, visible focus rings, immediate feedback
Flat-with-structure elevation — borders and subtle shadows distinguish layers without depth theater
A single font family (Inter) with weight + size contrast carrying all hierarchy

rules.name: The Careful Record
rules.body: Every screen is a page in a well-kept patient record — organized, legible, nothing out of place.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Semantic colors (green, yellow, red, blue) communicate status — and only status. Never apply them to decorative elements, section backgrounds, or brand moments.

rules.name: The One Anchor Rule
rules.body: Deep Forest Teal (#0f5c5c) is the only accent color. A second brand hue signals a hierarchy problem, not a palette gap.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter only. Weight, size, and color create all hierarchy. A second typeface introduces noise with no functional payoff.

rules.name: The No-Uppercase-Body Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is reserved for text-xs table headers and badge labels only. Sentence case everywhere else.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards rest flat with a border. Shadows appear only on hover or when a surface genuinely floats above the content layer.

rules.name: The No-Nested-Cards Rule
rules.body: A rounded-xl border inside another rounded-xl border is always wrong. Restructure the information hierarchy instead.

rules.name: The Confirm Before Delete Rule
rules.body: Every danger button must be preceded by a ConfirmDialog. Destructive actions never fire on first click.

rules.name: The Scannable Row Rule
rules.body: Primary entity name in the first column as font-medium. Metadata uses text-slate-500. Status badge in the last data column. No decorative columns.

dos: Do use Deep Forest Teal (#0f5c5c) for primary actions, active nav states, and focus rings only.
Do pair every badge color with text — a dot or icon alongside the label for color-blind users.
Do show a ConfirmDialog before every destructive mutation.
Do use rounded-xl for containers (cards, modals) and rounded-lg for interactive elements (buttons, inputs).
Do keep table headers uppercase text-xs tracking-wide and body cells text-sm with no case transformation.
Do add a visible focus ring (2px, #1a9e9e) on all interactive elements.
Do use text-wrap: balance on h1–h2 page headings.
donts: Don't use the EHR gray aesthetic — dense gray forms, tiny unlabeled inputs, overwhelming tables with no visual hierarchy.
Don't use consumer wellness aesthetics (pastel backgrounds, oversized whitespace, rounded-2xl everything).
Don't apply generic SaaS minimalism (all-white + blue accent monotony).
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards or callouts.
Don't apply gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient).
Don't nest cards. A card inside a card is always wrong.
Don't use #94a3b8 (ink-muted) for body-size text on white backgrounds.
Don't use uppercase for body copy or button labels.
Don't add section eyebrows (small all-caps kickers above every heading).
